outOfScope: Treating GitHub branch protection, required checks, PR approval or check-run naming as the ExHarness delivery state machine.
Rewriting Blackboard V2 Work/Attempt/CAS/lease/fence primitives owned by BB-155.
Changing JEV provider/model/verdict semantics or duplicating BB-157 LOOKBACK/material-delta supervision logic.
Migrating unfinished legacy tasks to V2; BB-156 owns cutover/migration.
Optimizing CI duration or parallelism without a measured verification dependency/latency baseline.
Implementing a vendor-specific CI platform abstraction beyond the minimal GitHub Actions adapter required to prove the canonical contract.
constraints: RESEARCH_SA first: opening BB-158 grants no CI implementation authority. Research must close with a fresh exact READY plan and independent JEV satisfaction before Worker mutation.

Blackboard V2 Work generation, Attempt, candidate/evidence identities and Decisions are canonical control authority; PR numbers, workflow names, check conclusions and branch-protection state are adapter metadata only.
CI is an execution and feedback plane, not an independent source of Work lifecycle truth or correctness authority.
Deterministic verifiers and semantic supervisors may publish into one typed observation/evidence model, but their authority classes remain distinct; JEV stays independent semantic supervision.
Every observation must bind the exact Work generation, Attempt and candidate/evidence subject it evaluated. Stale or superseded results fail closed and cannot advance delivery.
Retry is driven by failure class, material candidate/evidence delta and explicit retry policy, never by blind rerun-until-green behavior.
Progressive/early failure may cancel irrelevant downstream execution, but emitted evidence and accounting must remain truthful about completed, partial, cancelled and unavailable work.
GitHub Actions is one execution adapter. The contract must remain usable by local or future CI runtimes without re-defining delivery semantics.
invariants: A GitHub check conclusion never creates canonical readiness, correctness or repair authority.
Verification observations are immutable and exact-subject-bound; stale generation/Attempt/candidate/evidence results are non-authoritative.
Deterministic verification failure, verifier failure, infrastructure failure, suspected flake, cancellation and insufficient evidence remain distinct states.
A retry that can change delivery conclusions requires an allowed retry class or material candidate/evidence progress; control/prose-only churn cannot unlock product re-evaluation.
Early termination/cancellation preserves truthful partial execution and evidence accounting.
Local verification and CI execution consume the same canonical verification contract even when their transport/runtime differs.
JEV remains independent semantic supervision and consumes canonical candidate/evidence context rather than GitHub check state.
architectureDecisions: DRAFT D1 — Model CI as Verification Execution + Observation Publication, not a PR gate. Canonical lifecycle authority remains Blackboard V2.

DRAFT D2 — Introduce one candidate-bound verification observation family carrying workId, workGeneration, attemptId, candidate identity, verifier identity/class, subject, outcome, evidence refs/hashes, freshness, failure class and execution/accounting state.

DRAFT D3 — Keep deterministic verifiers and JEV as different authority classes behind the same evidence-routing boundary: deterministic observations prove executable checks; JEV publishes independent semantic Decisions.
DRAFT D4 — Add a verification planner that can order cheap/high-information checks first, publish terminally-known failures early and cancel dependent work while preserving truthful partial state.

DRAFT D5 — Route findings back through the delivery agent/Blackboard nextActions loop. Repair/retry eligibility derives from failure class plus material delta or an explicit bounded infra/flaky retry policy.
DRAFT D6 — Define selective re-verification from declared verification dependencies/affected subjects. Full repository verification remains a policy decision, not the only feedback primitive.
DRAFT D7 — Treat GitHub Actions as an adapter that executes planned verification and projects canonical state to checks/statuses. PR head/check-name/skip semantics cannot be canonical selectors.
DRAFT D8 — Delivery/merge projection consumes canonical current readiness/evidence and exact candidate binding; transport gates may block actuation but cannot manufacture readiness.
implementationSlices: R1 — Current-state audit: map workflow/script/local-verifier/delivery/JEV surfaces, current selectors, outputs, waits, retries and authority leaks; measure baseline latency and failure feedback timing.
R2 — Contract research: compare agent-native CI/execution patterns and ratify exact VerificationObservation/Evidence/failure taxonomy plus freshness and authority semantics.
R3 — Control-loop design: specify progressive execution, early terminal failure, cancellation, diagnosis/repair, bounded retry, selective re-verification, JEV handoff and convergence.
R4 — Adapter boundary: specify GitHub Actions input/output mapping and status projection without GitHub transport facts becoming canonical domain state.
R5 — Evaluation/decomposition: define adversarial fixtures and benchmark scenarios, then publish a fresh implementation plan only after research gaps are closed.

negativeVerificationCases: A green/skipped GitHub required check marks a candidate delivery-ready without canonical current verification evidence.
A verification result from a stale Work generation, Attempt or candidate is accepted after head/candidate movement.
A product-test failure, runner outage and suspected flaky failure collapse to the same retry behavior.
Control/prose-only changes cause another product/JEV evaluation despite no required material delta.
Early failure cancels downstream jobs but the published run is falsely reported as fully executed.
Selective re-verification reuses evidence whose declared subject/dependencies were invalidated by the candidate delta.
JEV derives semantic judgment from GitHub check status instead of exact candidate/evidence context.

researchGaps: Audit current main end to end: every workflow trigger/condition, verification script, JEV dispatch, local verifier, delivery finalizer, status projection and retry path.

Ratify the minimal typed VerificationObservation/ExecutionRun contract and failure taxonomy from primary-source agent-native CI/runtime patterns; public repository examples must meet the existing >=1000-star research rule.
Measure current feedback latency and identify which checks support early terminal failure, dependency cancellation and safe selective re-verification.
Define evidence invalidation/dependency semantics so selective re-verification cannot reuse stale proof.
Define how canonical V2 nextActions consume verification outcomes without adding a second hidden CI state machine.
Resolve the exact GitHub Actions projection contract and required-check behavior after BB-155 and BB-157 APIs are delivered.

livingDocs.statement: Living system state must describe CI as an agent-facing verification execution/feedback plane with exact candidate-bound evidence, explicit authority boundaries, progressive failure semantics and GitHub Actions as an adapter only after the contract is actually delivered.

valueHypothesis: Reducing CI from a human-oriented terminal gate to a machine-readable feedback/control plane should shorten agent failure-to-repair latency, eliminate PR/check-state authority leaks, and make autonomous delivery retries/re-verification more correct and cheaper. Research must measure these claims before optimization.
